script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this flow is inferred from two-game form only and is not a market script. GB profiles as the cleaner environment: Love is +0.16 EPA/dropback when not blitzed (n=46) and ATL blitzes only 21%, while Watson and Golden have taken 19 and 18 targets with 213 and 217 air yards. ATL has lived on Bijan (37 carries, 155 rush yards, 14 targets for 99 yards on -18 air yards) because Penix is negative EPA both vs blitz (-0.35, n=22) and off blitz (-0.80). Base read: GB functions through the two air-yard receivers, ATL stays checkdown-and-Bijan, and explosives lean GB (ATL 8 of 81, GB 2 of 72) without a priced lead or total.
script.flip1: ATL stays close or leads, Bijan holds an 18-20 carry role, and GB pass volume dips so Golden/Watson fall well short of 9 targets apiece.
script.flip2: GB gets ahead, ATL abandons the run into a 34% GB blitz, and a London or Pitts chunk (Pitts already has 52 air yards but only 15 receiving yards) becomes the ATL spike while GB receivers stall in a second-half run clock.

matchup.bleeds: ATL allows 8 passes of 20+ on 81 attempts and 14.12 YPA in the middle on only 8 attempts (left 5.14 on 36, right 6.36 on 33); rush defense 3.41 YPC with 2 runs of 10+. GB allows 2 passes of 20+ on 72 attempts, outside YPA 5.67 left (21 att) and 5.74 right (35 att), middle 9.75 on only 8 att, and 3.05 YPC with 3 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: GB's co-primary air-yard pair, Golden 217 air yards and Watson 213, overlaps ATL's explosive leakage and the thin middle sample, with Love's good no-blitz EPA against a 21% blitz. London (9 targets, 45 air yards, 80 yards) does not overlap a GB weak spot: GB's outside YPA is about 5.7 and explosives are 2 of 72.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because Watson (19 targets, 188 yards, 213 air yards) and Kraft (92 air yards) took the explosives ATL allows, GB protected a lead, and Golden finished on 6 targets around 50 yards, short of 55.5. London, stuck on 9 targets for 80 yards through two games, was the underfed WR1 and drew 8-plus targets; one of the two 20-plus gains GB has allowed on 72 throws was his, and 8 targets at his 8.9 yards per target is about 71, clearing 67. The counter is real because the samples are two games and the missing spread may already be in the 55.5 and 67, but it is not stronger than the read: Golden's line still sits about 21 yards under his pace and survives a modest target dip, and London still needs an explosive GB has produced on only 2 of 72 throws.
slip_story: One GB-functional-pass / ATL-explosives-suppressed story: Golden over belongs with GB's air-yard game against a 21% blitz and an explosive-leaky ATL defense, and London under belongs with the same GB defense that has allowed 2 explosives on 72 throws. Not a shootout stack, not a clock-kill RB stack, and not mixed with a total. Watson over 71.5 was left off because a dip to 7 targets at 9.9 yards per target lands near 69 and fails the flip test.
